title: Build a safe report path from one filename
prompt: Accept a single nonempty filename ending in .txt with no slash, backslash, or dot-dot name. Return root / filename as an optional path; reject a path or directory supplied as the filename. This is lexical validation for a trusted root, not a defense against symlinks in an untrusted directory.

tests.label: Valid leaf
tests.hint: Join the trusted root to the leaf name.

tests.label: Traversal rejected
tests.hint: A path separator means it is not one filename.

tests.label: Absolute rejected
tests.hint: A filename cannot supply its own root.

hints: Validate the filename text before joining it.
path.extension() examines the suffix of the one remaining leaf.
explanation: filesystem::path joins path parts without hand-written separators. Lexical validation is suitable when the root directory itself is trusted; secure access to an untrusted tree needs OS-level checks.
